title: Casper and the Alibi
premise: When the coffin of town founder Elias Wren is found empty during a civic exhumation, retired detective Sable Sandoval realizes the empty grave matches a pattern he's spent twelve years ignoring: missing persons his old cases quietly closed. A coded ledger, hidden in the accounting books of Wren's original general store—now Sable's bookshop—points to a survival pact among the town's founding families, one that required disappearances to keep it funded. As Sable decodes the ledger, he discovers his late wife was the pact's record-keeper and that his own silence after her death made him complicit. In the end, Sable exposes the surviving conspirators at the town's centennial gala, chooses truth over the loyalty that protected him, and reopens the graves—literally and figuratively—at the cost of the only community he had left.
about_author: Ada Okafor is a former forensic accountant who traded audit trails for plot twists after a decade of uncovering small-town financial crimes. She writes mysteries from a converted canal boat, where she keeps her own ledger of every lie her characters tell.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Dirt
chapters.summary: Sable Sandoval, POV. During the centennial exhumation of founder Elias Wren, the coffin is revealed to be empty except for a child's shoe. The crowd gasps; Sable alone notices the mayor's hands shaking. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm—the instinct he thought he'd buried waking up.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Back at his failing bookshop—the former Wren General Store—he catalogs what he knows about the town's founding families while deflecting the new sheriff's questions. He finds faint columned notations penciled inside the store's original ledgers. Beat: unease curdling into recognition; the past has been shelved beside him for years.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Sable, POV, with a flashback to his wife Marisol teaching him her grandmother's substitution cipher over card games. He confirms the pencil marks are prices that aren't prices—a running tally of payments. Beat: grief and excitement braided together as the shop becomes a crime scene of paper.

chapters.title: The Sheriff Who Wasn't Asking
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dana Ito, POV. Ito investigates the empty grave but is quietly ordered by the council to close it as 'settling soil.' She notices Sable's name appearing in twelve-year-old case files. Beat: institutional pressure versus conscience; she decides to watch Sable rather than suspect him—for now.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Closed Doors
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. He pulls his own cold cases from memory: three missing persons, all filed as runaways, all connected to founding-family businesses. Each closure bears his signature. Beat: shame surfacing; the reader learns Sable didn't just keep secrets—he certified them.

chapters.title: The Shoe That Didn't Fit
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Forensics dates the child's shoe to roughly 1968, decades before Wren's recorded death. Sable realizes the coffin was a decoy from the start—Wren may never have been buried at all. Beat: vertigo; the town's origin story is a constructed object, like a staged room.

chapters.title: What Marisol Kept
chapters.summary: Sable, POV, interleaved with Marisol's journal entries (her voice). He finds her hidden deposit box containing a duplicate cipher key and a note: 'If you're reading this, stop counting.' Beat: betrayal and tenderness; she protected him by excluding him, and it worked too well.

chapters.title: The Founders' Table
chapters.summary: Mayor Corliss Hale, POV. At a closed-door council meeting, Hale pressures the remaining founding heirs to hold the line, revealing she knows someone is decoding the ledger. Beat: menace under civility; the conspiracy is smaller, older, and more frightened than Sable imagined.

chapters.title: Runaway Number Four
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. A fourth disappearance—one even Sable never closed—surfaces: a bookkeeper who vanished in 1994, the year the ledger's entries stop. Her sister, Ruth Okafor-Adeyemi, arrives in town asking questions. Beat: hope with an edge; an ally who owes the town nothing.

chapters.title: Decoding the Debt
chapters.summary: Sable and Ruth, alternating POV. Working nights in the shop, they crack the ledger's structure: each entry pairs a payment with a name reduced to initials. The initials belong to living townspeople. Beat: mounting horror; the pact isn't history—it's payroll, possibly still active.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. The shop is searched; the original ledgers are nearly stolen. Sable baits the thief with a fake page and catches a glimpse of the courier: quiet, beloved hardware-store owner Tomás Reyes. Beat: paranoia sharpening into strategy; Sable stops being prey.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Currency
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. Under gentle pressure from Sable, Tomás confesses he's been paid for thirty years to keep the store's back room sealed—and that his own brother was one of the disappeared. Beat: tragic complicity; loyalty as both cage and ransom.

chapters.title: The Back Room
chapters.summary: Sable, Ruth, and Tomás, POV. Behind a false wall they find boxes: belongings of the disappeared, Wren's real death certificate dated 1971, and evidence the 'pact' began as a mutual-aid fund that curdled into blackmail. Beat: revelation as excavation; the town's kindness was always double-entry.

chapters.title: Ito Closes In
chapters.summary: Sheriff Ito, POV. Following the theft report, Ito finds Sable's decoy page and confronts him—not to arrest him but to force him to choose between going public or becoming another keeper of the file. Beat: collision of two honest people on opposite sides of procedure.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. He reconstructs the full mechanism: families bought silence with the aid fund, and the disappeared were those who threatened to expose it—including, he now understands, people Marisol tried to save. Beat: devastation; his wife's secrecy reframed as resistance, and his own retirement as surrender.

chapters.title: An Offer, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Mayor Hale, POV. Hale offers Sable a place on the council, the shop's deed free and clear, and the original ledgers 'for the archive.' She invokes his wife's name. Beat: temptation rendered precisely; the same deal Marisol must have refused.

chapters.title: What Marisol Refused
chapters.summary: Sable, POV, with Marisol's final journal pages. He learns she died in a car accident three days before she planned to deliver copies to the state attorney. The brake line was inspected and cleared. Beat: cold fury; grief converts to purpose.

chapters.title: Centennial Eve
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Ruth, Tomás, Ito). The allies prepare: copies duplicated, witnesses lined up, Ito formally requesting state investigators despite the council. Sabotage strikes—the shop catches fire overnight. Beat: breathless preparation shadowed by loss; the enemy is listening.

chapters.title: Ashes and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Surveying the burned shop, he finds the fire consumed everything except the safe where Marisol's journal survived. Ruth reveals she mailed a second copy out of town days ago. Beat: rebirth through ruin; what matters was never the paper.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. At the centennial gala, before the town and the state investigators Ito smuggled in, Sable reads the ledger aloud—names, payments, initials—then names the living conspirators, including Hale and the town doctor. Beat: climax; truth spoken in the temple of the lie.

chapters.title: Reopening the Grave
chapters.summary: Sheriff Ito, POV. Arrests ripple outward; the state team orders the Wren plot fully excavated and finds a second coffin beneath—Elias Wren himself, murdered in 1971 by the first pact members. Beat: grim vindication; the ground finally gives up its testimony.

chapters.title: Shelving Order
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Months later, the rebuilt shop reopens with a memorial shelf for the disappeared, their names restored to the record. Ruth stays; Tomás testifies; Sable files his last secret—Marisol's journal—with the state archive. Beat: bittersweet resolution; he chose truth over belonging and built a smaller, honest belonging in its place.
